what: HWSD v2.0 data model (from the manual)
title: tidyhwsd: full tutorial
text: HWSD v2.0 built around global grid soil mapping units (SMU). grid provided 30 arc-second (~1 km) raster ESRI BIL format. grid cell stores SMU identifier links attribute tables. SMU can contain multiple components. component, manual defines: SEQUENCE: ordering components (sequence 1 dominant) SHARE: percent share within SMU (sums ~100) LAYER: depth layer, seven standard layers (D1-D7) seven layers correspond 0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-150, 150-200 cm.

what: How tidyhwsd maps the manual to code
title: tidyhwsd: full tutorial
text: hwsd_download() retrieves raster grid (BIL) used SMU indexing. hwsd2_layers component table keyed HWSD2_SMU_ID, LAYER, SEQUENCE, SHARE. hwsd2 pre-collapsed SMU x layer attribute table. hwsd_extract() returns dominant-component values default (compatible legacy workflows). hwsd_compose() performs share-weighted synthesis using rules hwsd_props(). want work directly components (e.g., custom aggregation), start hwsd2_layers.

title: tidyhwsd: full tutorial
text: HWSD manual notes SMU may contain multiple soil components. two common ways summarize : Dominant values represent dominant component (sequence 1, largest share). Composed values use component shares compute weighted summaries. hwsd_extract() uses dominant component default. consistent many legacy workflows avoids misleading averages small share extreme value. need share-weighted summary, use hwsd_compose() rules hwsd_props(). Dominant selection logic: Prefer SEQUENCE = 1 present Within SEQUENCE = 1, pick largest SHARE SEQUENCE = 1 exists, pick largest SHARE

title: tidyhwsd: full tutorial
text: hwsd_extract() returns dominant-component values default. share-weighted composition, use hwsd_compose() rules hwsd_props(): Default aggregation rules (hwsd_props()): Numeric fields use weighted_mean Categorical fields use weighted_mode ID-like fields drop Numeric outputs rounded precision step Negative numeric values treated missing, shares normalized sum 100.
code: props <- hwsd_props() pt_syn <- hwsd_compose(   coords = c(110, 40),   param = c("SAND", "PH_WATER"),   layer = "D1",   ws_path = "~/data/HWSD2",   props = props )

title: tidyhwsd: full tutorial
text: can override aggregation per-variable basis. example, keep pH dominant averaging textures: can also pass named vector quick overrides: hwsd_extract(props = ...) equivalent hwsd_compose() can used keep single entry point:
code: props <- hwsd_props() props$agg[props$property == "PH_WATER"] <- "dominant"  pt_mixed <- hwsd_compose(   coords = c(110, 40),   param = c("SAND", "PH_WATER"),   layer = "D1",   ws_path = "~/data/HWSD2",   props = props ) agg <- c(PH_WATER = "dominant", SAND = "weighted_mean") pt_named <- hwsd_compose(   coords = c(110, 40),   param = c("SAND", "PH_WATER"),   layer = "D1",   ws_path = "~/data/HWSD2",   props = agg ) props <- hwsd_props() props$agg[props$property == "PH_WATER"] <- "dominant" pt_syn2 <- hwsd_extract(   coords = c(110, 40),   param = c("SAND", "PH_WATER"),   layer = "D1",   ws_path = "~/data/HWSD2",   props = props )

title: tidyhwsd: full tutorial
text: large areas, enable tiling improve performance: Regional extraction notes: Bbox queries return terra::SpatRaster; point queries return tibble. Use internal = FALSE write GeoTIFFs disk (returns output path). Windows, cores falls back sequential processing (parallel used non-Windows). need categorical rasters (e.g., DRAINAGE), request explicitly rather using param = "".

what: Data model (from the HWSD v2.0 manual)
title: HWSD v2.0 units and aggregation
text: HWSD v2.0 stores soil information per soil mapping unit (SMU). SMU can 12 components, : SEQUENCE: order components (sequence 1 dominant) SHARE: percent share, summed 100 within SMU LAYER: D1 D7 depth layers hwsd2_layers component table; hwsd_extract() hwsd_compose() map SMU IDs attributes using fields.

title: HWSD v2.0 units and aggregation
text: hwsd_props() provides description default aggregation rule property, plus precision field encodes rounding step used aggregation. Common units (manual field definitions): Depth: TOPDEP, BOTDEP cm (D1 = 0-20 cm; …; D7 = 150-200 cm) Texture: SAND, SILT, CLAY percent weight Bulk density: BULK, REF_BULK g/cm3 Organic carbon: ORG_CARBON percent weight pH: PH_WATER water (-log(H+)) Total nitrogen: TOTAL_N g/kg CEC / ECEC / TEB: cmol/kg Electrical conductivity: ELEC_COND dS/m AWC: AWC mm/m (see manual table USDA texture classes) Code fields: ROOT_DEPTH class code (1-4; deep shallow) ROOTS, IL, SWR class codes (see manual) DRAINAGE categorical class

title: HWSD v2.0 units and aggregation
text: hwsd_extract() returns dominant component values: SEQUENCE = 1 preferred within SEQUENCE = 1, largest SHARE chosen SEQUENCE = 1 exists, largest SHARE chosen hwsd_compose() performs share-weighted synthesis using rules hwsd_props(): numeric fields: weighted_mean categorical fields: weighted_mode ID-like fields: drop numeric outputs rounded precision step Example:
code: props <- hwsd_props() props$agg[props$property == "PH_WATER"] <- "dominant"  pt_dom <- hwsd_extract(   coords = c(110, 40),   param = c("PH_WATER", "SAND"),   layer = "D1",   ws_path = "D:/data/HWSD2" )  pt_syn <- hwsd_compose(   coords = c(110, 40),   param = c("PH_WATER", "SAND"),   layer = "D1",   ws_path = "D:/data/HWSD2",   props = props )

title: tidyhwsd 0.2.0
text: Default extraction returns dominant components match legacy behavior. Added composition workflow via hwsd_compose() aggregation rules hwsd_props(). Expanded property metadata precision clarified units. Updated documentation examples reflect dominant vs. composed outputs.
